The reason this stuff is 'news' now is because that's what the public has shown it wanted. People want to turn on the news any hour of the day, and learn about current events.

That seems fine. Just have news going on often, and people will want to watch it. Then, every news station is mediocre. There is plain newscasters, normal stories, and facts presented from objective views. I think that's why a lot of news stations 20-30 years ago felt the need to spice things up with things like "Where in the world is Matt Lauer".

What do they do to get ahead? More attractive hosts. Stories that catch peoples attention. Outrage culture. People love to get angry at things. There's a great video about this that will be linked at the bottom. When people get angry about something, they remember it. Couple this idea of trying to get the viewer to react/get angry and corporopolitical interests and you get the biased, low quality news that we see today.

Online news is somewhat isolated from most of the factors that cause this, except for the reactionary part. Far left and right journalist newspapers often have comment sections full with people angry together.

Relevant links:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rE3j_RHkqJc
http://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LowestCommonDenominator

It's because most people --myself often included-- don't really decide logically what should be news to them. For example someone getting killed speaks to us un some more primal level. The moment we hear someone's life was ended there is a part in us that thinks 'holy shit, i have to know more about this, it could happen to me too'. That's why reporting on crime such a hot topic.

Someone being locked up in a basement by some psycho concerns almost noone directly. The risk that it happens to someone is almost nil. Still the emotional impact of it is so high. What if it happened to me? That's why news that are rather more abstract but actually concern people get less traction.

Climate changing ? Probably happening so slowly that it doesn't command immediate attention. New union laws - meh... Someone getting dismembered by a psycho with a table spoon ? Holy shit I've gotta see this.

It's a pretty stupid pattern, but we instictively seek out news about sex, danger, violence and death because we are instinctively biased to look for information like that. Capturing attention with news like this is just easier...
